name: Tensorlake

facts.value: Tensorlake Cloud
facts.notes: Free, Usage Credits, Pro, and Enterprise plans are documented for the hosted service.

facts.value: Customer-operated sandbox executors and optional Sandbox Proxy; Tensorlake Cloud control plane
facts.notes: AWS install guide requires Self-hosted Compute enabled on the project (contact Tensorlake if unavailable), supported bare-metal EC2 with KVM/local NVMe, S3, and optional EKS/NLB/customer TLS ingress. This is hybrid self-hosted compute, not a documented independent control-plane install. Enterprise pricing advertises on-prem; security docs offer fully disconnected on-prem by contact, with public deployment details and commercial terms unresolved.

facts.value: AWS documented install; vendor also advertises GCP, Azure, CoreWeave, Nebius, and bare metal
facts.notes: Customer owns compute/storage; Tensorlake Cloud remains scheduling/auth control plane. AWS requires Self-hosted Compute enablement and onboarding; proxy can be Tensorlake-operated over VPC peering or customer-operated. Enterprise pricing lists In-VPC/on-prem. Other clouds are official commercial claims, not verified install paths. Do not infer ungated public-plan access or fully self-hosted service.

facts.value: Python and TypeScript; Rust sandbox client also documented in the official SDK repository
facts.notes: Public runtime reference covers Python/TypeScript; official source documents Rust SandboxesClient, without full parity. SDK languages are not guest runtimes. The official-source inventory reviewed does not document a vendor-maintained Go Sandbox SDK as of 2026-10-08. A separately maintained community Go client exists (see community_sdk_languages and the dated official-source review); it is not evidence of vendor support or endorsement. The former no-official-Go conclusion was a bounded documented-support inference, not a vendor denial.

facts.value: TypeScript: ComputeSDK Tensorlake provider (@computesdk/tensorlake); Go: Sixt/tensorlake-go
facts.notes: Positive community client evidence: vendor-hosted tensorlakeai/computesdk fork includes the TypeScript Tensorlake adapter README/package/implementation. Separately maintained Sixt/tensorlake-go README describes a Go client for Tensorlake cloud sandbox create, process, PTY, suspend/resume, and snapshot APIs, with go get installation. Neither is vendor-maintained or evidence of official support/endorsement; no release-to-current-service compatibility test was performed. This is a verified example inventory, not an exhaustive list. The adapter does not override current platform ingress/snapshot restrictions.

facts.value: Available
facts.notes: Examples use https://api.tensorlake.ai/sandboxes. An OpenAPI spec is linked from the docs index.

facts.value: tl
facts.notes: Examples include tl sbx create, suspend, resume, checkpoint, and copy.

facts.value: Linux userland from the selected image
facts.notes: Managed Ubuntu minimal/systemd and Debian 13 images; ubuntu-vnc where desktop automation is enabled. Guest languages depend on installed image tools, not SDK languages. Custom images must be registered before launch.

facts.value: Hosted docs describe Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor microVMs; BYOC can use gVisor without KVM
facts.notes: MicroVMs have separate kernels. The BYOC announcement explicitly uses Firecracker where KVM is available and gVisor containers where it is not; do not generalize the microVM boundary to every customer deployment.

facts.value: Linux: managed Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13; custom Linux images
facts.notes: ubuntu-minimal is default, ubuntu-systemd supports services, ubuntu-vnc is desktop-gated. No Windows/macOS guest support established.

facts.value: Default 1 vCPU. Free max 1. Usage Credits max 4. Pro max 16. Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Per-sandbox caps, not dedicated physical cores. Lifecycle cpus is a float and says resources fixed after create. Official SDK repository documents live whole-vCPU resizing only for running Cloud Hypervisor sandboxes; hosted runtime/access applicability unresolved.

facts.value: Default 1024 MB in lifecycle; Free max 1 GB, Usage Credits 16 GB, Pro 64 GB; Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Paid plans also require 1-8 GB RAM per vCPU; both ratio and plan ceiling apply, so the ratio is not a 128 GB Pro entitlement. Lifecycle says 1024-8192 MB per CPU, create API says MiB, and billing usage says GiB-hours. No GB-to-GiB conversion. SDK repository documents runtime-gated Cloud Hypervisor resizing in 128 MiB blocks, unlike lifecycle's fixed-resource statement.

facts.value: Default 10240 MiB (10 GiB); create API range 10240-102400 MiB (10-100 GiB)
facts.notes: Billing plan caps say Free 10 GB and paid 100 GB; rates per GB-hour. Images/filesystem restores permit growth-only disk overrides. Lifecycle says resources fixed after creation, while SDK repository documents running Cloud Hypervisor growth-only disk resize. Pools docs say server-managed root disk/ignored ephemeral_disk_mb; repository README now describes disk_mb pool growth, so pool override applicability is unresolved.

facts.value: Conditional BYOC GPU sandbox offering; hosted GPU availability unresolved
facts.notes: Official BYOC announcement publishes GPU platform fees but no complete GPU capacity/access matrix. Current official SDK model enum accepts A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100, T4, A6000, A10, RTX-PRO-6000 and L40 requests. Client defaults gpus to A10 unless model supplied; GPU sandboxes require a content-addressed streaming (CAS) image, or server-configured GPU default if image omitted. Matching server/dataplane support and hardware capacity still required. Model/request syntax or CUDA image does not establish hosted entitlement, limits, region availability or a public GPU rate.

facts.value: Build from Dockerfile/Python/TypeScript or import public/private OCI images; register before launch
facts.notes: Unregistered registry launch unsupported; private pulls use Docker config/login credentials. Custom USER/WORKDIR applies, not managed defaults. FROM substitution not working, ONBUILD ignored; SHELL/EXPOSE/HEALTHCHECK/LABEL/STOPSIGNAL/VOLUME no runtime effect. New base preparation slower; builder defaults 2 vCPU/4096 MB and generated disk 10240 MiB. Current docs offer --docker_compat BuildKit fallback with at least 3x builder disk/memory. Register existing filesystem snapshot only when Completed with durable snapshot_uri, not local-ready/uploading. Harbor public publishing requires account allowlist unlike general guide's ungated wording; full architecture/size/access matrix unknown.

facts.value: Runtime installs and reusable image builds
facts.notes: Managed Ubuntu/Debian Python follows PEP 668: use a virtualenv or --break-system-packages. Apt installation needs guest sudo/root and permitted dependency egress. Preinstall dependencies before deny-all execution.

facts.value: Managed images use tl-user with passwordless sudo; explicit guest root execution supported
facts.notes: Guest privileges, not host privileges. Managed commands start at /, which is not generally writable by tl-user; use /home/tl-user or explicit workdir. Built/imported images follow Dockerfile USER/WORKDIR. Process APIs support user selection.

facts.value: Install Docker/Compose inside tensorlake/ubuntu-systemd
facts.notes: Requires systemd-capable image and guest sudo/root for installation; ubuntu-minimal excludes systemd. Harbor single-container tasks do not provide Docker; Compose uses a DinD host and does not support snapshot_id. Registry-image support is not Docker-in-Docker by itself.

facts.value: start_process/startProcess, signals, streaming and optional supervised restarts
facts.notes: Detached work continues after call return, but CPU/process activity alone is not established as preventing proxy-idle suspension; suspended processes make no progress. Lifecycle says open SSH/PTY proxy traffic counts; June networking blog says only transferred bytes count and idle-open connections do not. Do not rely on an idle connected terminal as keepalive; use actual traffic or appropriate timeout. Disconnected PTYs separately expire after 300 seconds.

facts.value: SDK/HTTP read/write/list/delete and CLI file copy
facts.notes: Management proxy port 9501 always requires auth. tl sbx cp is file-only; directory workflows use SDK/API or native SSH scp/rsync. Managed /workspace is not tl-user-writable without setup, despite file-page examples.

facts.value: Named suspend retains root files; independent snapshots or durable mounted filesystems recover files into replacements
facts.notes: Root disk is otherwise ephemeral. Restart within 48 hours restores the most recent usable snapshot, not necessarily final files; without one it cold-boots a fresh filesystem. Security docs say sandbox deletion permanently removes files/state while retaining separate snapshots; SDK/FAQ call termination final, conflicting with lifecycle/restart API. Durable mounts require explicit creation/attachment and recover acknowledged autosaves, not necessarily unreplicated writes. /tmp is documented as excluded from filesystem snapshots.

facts.value: Separate durable versioned POSIX filesystem mounts; Git workspace mounts have different publication semantics
facts.notes: Create filesystem before attaching; up to 8 absolute non-nested mounts per sandbox. Disjoint paths merge, same-path writes last-writer-wins. Server autosave WAL retains the newest 256 generations and all generations from the last 24 hours; permanent snapshots are separately billed until deleted. After a crash, remounting on another machine recovers through the last acknowledged server autosave, not unreplicated tail writes; on the same machine, its overlay/local journal can also recover unsaved changes. Current reviewed session/introduction docs do not establish per-filesystem session or session-metadata caps, precise crash-detection or salvage intervals, or eager-GC timing, so those numeric/behavioral limits remain unverified rather than zero or unlimited. Pins require read-only permanent snapshots/latest fleet support; invalid runtime attach can terminate sandbox. Git private WAL (30 seconds) is not branch commit; reattach explicit workspace. Complete volume/Git storage and I/O rates unresolved.

facts.value: Named sandboxes only; snapshot-backed suspension and resume
facts.notes: Ephemeral sandboxes cannot suspend and terminate on timeout. Named idle/manual suspend checkpoints state then terminates the live container; resume restores under the same logical sandbox name/ID, potentially another host. It is not indefinitely reserved host RAM. Suspend/resume return 202 on initiation; wait/poll for settled readiness, and resume fails if suspend snapshot missing/not ready. No compute charge suspended, but snapshot storage billed; open connections are dropped and clients must reconnect.

facts.value: Named suspend snapshot can restore memory and processes; not uninterrupted connections
facts.notes: Suspend is snapshot-plus-live-container teardown; named resume retains logical identity but may use another host. Captured process memory is restored, not running while suspended; external TCP sessions do not stay connected and reconnect/placement readiness required. Missing/not-ready suspend snapshot prevents resume. Independent filesystem checkpoint default cold-boots and does not preserve process memory; explicit memory checkpoint is different.

facts.value: filesystem (default, cold boot) and memory (filesystem, memory and processes, warm restore) checkpoints
facts.notes: Reusable artifacts outlive source termination; restore creates new sandbox. Current SDK checkpoint waits for local_ready by default (resumable), not necessarily completed with durable snapshot_uri metadata; wait_until=completed for that boundary. Memory restore cannot override image, CPU/memory resources, entrypoint or secrets per restore API; secret store linkage still unverified. Filesystem restore can change resources and grow disk only; /tmp excluded per PTY docs. SDK overview overstates generic memory preservation; Harbor Compose cannot use snapshot_id. Closed external connections are not revived by memory restore. Complete standalone retention/billing unresolved.

facts.value: CLI/HTTP warm copy; Python and TypeScript copy methods present in current official SDK source
facts.notes: Snapshot docs say CLI/HTTP copies from running or suspended source inherit image/resources/entrypoint/network/exposed ports and create no reusable checkpoint; inspect individual failures/unique names. Those docs say Python unsupported/TypeScript unexposed, but current official repository implements Sandbox.copy in both languages plus Python SandboxClient.copy(times=...). Source docstrings describe running-source live copy. Published-package version and deployed-server parity not established; do not assert all SDK versions support it or unsupported universally. No measured clone/reset latency or guaranteed capacity.

facts.value: Enabled by default; configurable deny-all or destination policy
facts.notes: allow_internet_access=false with empty allow_out blocks all outbound traffic including DNS. Non-empty allow_out is default-deny regardless of that flag; true permits resolver DNS, false requires resolver IP explicitly allowed for hostname resolution. CLI --no-internet cannot combine allow/deny flags. This does not remove separately authenticated management, SSH or inbound/tunnel paths.

facts.value: Host-enforced allow_out/deny_out with deny precedence and dynamic updates
facts.notes: Allow domains, leading-wildcard subdomains (not apex), IPv4/CIDRs; deny docs no wildcards, Harbor no IPv6. Current SDK model says optional :port suffix accepted but not port-specific. Host firewall blog uses readable TCP SNI/HTTP Host without TLS termination, IP/CIDR fallback for unreadable names, DNS-derived TTL rules for UDP/ICMP/QUIC, internal addresses only explicit literals. No blanket security guarantee. Conflicts: networking closes old flows/rejects unresolved names; Harbor and update API say old connections continue; Aug29 blog fences old flows but accepts unresolved allow names and may terminate on failed enforcement. Blog wildcard deny conflicts with docs. Current SDK model also says established/related always allowed. Exact deployed behavior/version unresolved; SDK>=0.5.133 needed to read network_policy reliably.

facts.value: HTTPS proxy to explicitly exposed user services; native SSH and authenticated local TCP tunnels are separate
facts.notes: https://<port>-<id-or-name>.sandbox.tensorlake.ai forwards HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC/HTTP2 only if port is in exposed_ports (API range 1-65535; management 9501 reserved/auth always). User ports default to project API-key auth; explicit allow_unauthenticated_access makes exposed ports public, and CLI port expose does both. Named suspended sandboxes may auto-resume on ingress. Prefer returned ingress_endpoint for placement/BYOC. Raw TCP requires a caller-local authenticated WebSocket tunnel (default bind 127.0.0.1), not general public raw-TCP exposure; native SSH uses registered user keys. No universal service bind-address requirement is stated.

facts.value: HTTPS sandbox service URLs usable for temporary previews
facts.notes: Networking explicitly lists preview environments at https://<port>-<id-or-name>.sandbox.tensorlake.ai. Service must listen inside the sandbox and the user port must be exposed; project API-key/browser-session auth by default, public only with allow_unauthenticated_access. Management 9501 never public. URLs depend on placement and sandbox lifecycle; named suspended ingress may auto-resume, not a durable deployment or raw-TCP endpoint.

facts.value: Gated BYOC VPC execution with Tensorlake-peered or customer-operated ingress
facts.notes: AWS guide keeps executors and S3 in customer account but Tensorlake Cloud control plane remains. Self-hosted Compute enablement/onboarding required; Enterprise markets In-VPC/on-prem. Customer ingress needs EKS/NLB/public DNS/ACM HTTPS, so do not call the endpoint private by default. No general hosted sandbox-to-sandbox private network established. BYOC blog advertises other clouds without equivalent public install detail.

facts.value: Free 1; Usage Credits up to 100; Pro 1,000; Enterprise unlimited (commercial plan limits)
facts.notes: Not guaranteed immediate capacity or API throughput. 5-million-per-project/24,000 scheduled per second BYOC claims are platform scale, not public hosted quotas. Create can queue; bare-metal host boot up to 20 minutes. Pools cap warm+claimed containers and cold-start if warm buffer empty. No numeric API request-rate limit found.

facts.value: Published plan durations: Free 2 hours, Usage Credits 24 hours, Pro/Enterprise unlimited; wall-clock cap unresolved
facts.notes: Billing calls these maximum session durations, but lifecycle explicitly says timeout_secs is proxy-idle threshold, not wall-clock lifetime, bounded by those plan maxima; 0 requests plan maximum. Create OpenAPI also lists Free unverified 1 hour / verified 2 hours and old On-Demand naming. Do not infer a fixed active lifetime or ignore verification gate. SDK repository resize guide/Harbor loosely call timeout lifetime/hard timeout, conflicting with lifecycle.

facts.value: Default 600-second proxy-idle threshold; exact connection activity signal conflicting
facts.notes: Named idle suspend preserves captured state; ephemeral terminates. Lifecycle says no in-flight proxied traffic and lists open SSH/WebSocket PTY as activity; June 17 networking blog says bytes actually transferred reset idle, an open silent connection does not pin sandbox. Do not guarantee idle-open terminals or detached CPU jobs keep alive. Free published max 2 hours (API unverified 1 hour), Usage Credits 24 hours, Pro/Enterprise unlimited; 0 requests maximum. Disconnected PTY cleanup separately 300 seconds. Exact wall-clock/idle activity enforcement unresolved across official sources.

Numeric request-rate quota remains unknown after official docs/marketing/OpenAPI/SDK second pass and targeted quota/429/rate searches as of 2026-10-08 (Q02/Q13 and eligibility ledger). Concurrent sandboxes, 64 concurrent PTYs and scheduler throughput are different quantities. Numeric absence is not zero, unlimited or unsupported HTTP/API capability under the eligibility policy.

Official July 21 multi-cloud scheduling article advertises project pinning to specific region/cloud/VPC and commercial July 28 BYOC article offers specific-VPC or EU-geo placement. This establishes a vendor placement claim, not a complete hosted selectable-region list or plan/access guarantee; article diagrams/examples are not a public availability matrix. EU API docs example is Workflows and filesystem eu-central-1 is storage, not sandbox compute. Restores need eligible snapshot-region executor; AWS BYOC uses customer's supported region. Full compute region/entitlement matrix remains unknown.

facts.value: stdout/stderr or combined output over SSE; SDK iterators and CLI streaming
facts.notes: follow_output/followOutput stream tracked processes through authenticated sandbox management ingress.

facts.value: Retained searchable sandbox stdout/stderr via Console, SDK, CLI and HTTP
facts.notes: Separate from per-process output buffers. Filter level, stable process ID or body text; structured attributes returned but not independent query filters. Retention depends on environment policy; no universal sandbox log-retention duration verified. Orchestration tracing is separate.

facts.value: Native SSH and reconnectable programmatic PTY over WebSocket
facts.notes: Native SSH key registration uses user auth, not API key; CLI ssh is PTY, not native forwarding/file transfer. PTY API auth plus attach token; create API documents max 64 concurrent PTY sessions per sandbox (429 when reached), separate from sandbox concurrency/API throughput. Disconnect leaves shell until independent 300-second no-client cleanup. Remote SSH supported; /tmp excluded from filesystem snapshots. Idle-open connection preventing sandbox suspension is conflicting across lifecycle/networking blog.

Create OpenAPI declares secret_names for sandbox injection and restore API says memory-checkpoint secrets cannot be changed on restore; no verified managed store linkage, provisioning, rotation or access guarantees. Current official Python create signature and Rust create model omit secret_names, reinforcing API/SDK surface skew rather than absence. Ordinary env maps exist; Crabbox integration allowlists local shell secrets with --allow-env, injects for one command then removes them, not a vendor managed secret store. applications/secrets encrypted @function store is Orchestration scope and cannot establish sandbox management. Full sandbox-managed design remains unknown.

facts.value: Project-scoped API keys and sandbox proxy auth; Enterprise advertises SSO/SAML/RBAC
facts.notes: SDK/REST keys select project and inherit project-member permissions; management port 9501 always auth, user ports can be explicitly public. Browser proxy accepts session cookie plus project/org; proxy strips platform cookie. SSO requires organization enablement/admin, supports OIDC/SAML and does not revoke API keys; bypass admins retain password login. Access-control docs contradict themselves on member key-creation permission; BYOC project-admin key terminology also conflicts with generic key docs. Pro+ HIPAA/BAA is commercial compliance, not secret management.

facts.value: Harbor, Claude Managed Agents, OpenCode, Cursor Cloud Agents, Devin Outposts, computer use, Chrome CDP
facts.notes: Listed in the docs index and homepage.

facts.value: Apache-2.0 for the official tensorlakeai/tensorlake repository
facts.notes: The official repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0, and its README documents the Sandbox API/client and CLI. This establishes the license of that public source repository, not that every production Sandbox control-plane/runtime component is included or that the complete hosted service can be self-hosted. The prior unsupported conclusion concerned the broader deployable service/runtime and was too broad for this field; exact service component boundaries remain unverified.

network_isolation.note: Host-enforced deny-all with allow_internet_access=false and empty allow_out includes DNS; egress is open by default. Ingress/SSH/authenticated tunnels are separate. Dynamic update connection/resolution behavior conflicts across networking, Harbor and firewall blog; not a blanket isolation guarantee.

egress_allowlist.note: Non-empty allow_out default-deny; leading wildcard excludes apex, IPv4/CIDRs, deny precedence/no denywildcards per docs. Resolver DNS conditional. Current SDK :port suffix not port-specific; Harbor no IPv6. TCP hostname vs UDP/QUIC enforcement differs. Update API/SDK established-flow permission conflicts with networking close-old-flow claim.

inbound_ports_or_preview_urls.note: HTTPS/WS/gRPC routes only explicitly exposed user ports at https://<port>-<sandbox-id-or-name>.sandbox.tensorlake.ai; project auth by default, public only with allow_unauthenticated_access. Management 9501 always auth. Raw TCP uses separate caller-local authenticated tunnels. Named suspended services can auto-resume; use returned ingress_endpoint for placement.

private_networking.note: AWS BYOC VPC execution requires Self-hosted Compute enablement/onboarding; Tensorlake Cloud control plane remains. Proxy may be Tensorlake-peered or customer-operated with EKS/NLB/public HTTPS domain. General hosted private networking is unresolved; Enterprise advertises In-VPC/on-prem.

snapshots.note: Filesystem default cold-boots; memory captures files/memory/processes, not external connection continuity. SDK local_ready default is resumable; completed required for durable snapshot_uri metadata/image registration. /tmp excluded from filesystem snapshots. Memory image/CPU/memory/entrypoint/secrets fixed per restore API; managed secret store still unverified. Harbor Compose no snapshot_id; complete retention/billing unresolved.

memory_snapshot_or_live_resume.note: Named suspend checkpoints files/memory/processes then tears down live container; resume logical identity may use another host. Processes do not advance suspended, external connections dropped; missing/not-ready snapshot prevents resume. Explicit memory checkpoint differs from default filesystem cold boot.

pause_resume.note: Named only; snapshot-backed suspension frees live container/compute, not indefinitely reserved host RAM. Resume same logical ID/name may use another host and requires ready suspend snapshot. 202 means initiated, not settled; clients reconnect. Storage still billed; ephemeral cannot suspend.

cloning_forking.note: CLI/HTTP warm copy documented; current official Python and TypeScript source both expose Sandbox.copy. Snapshot docs still say unsupported/unexposed; released-package version/server parity unknown. Source docstrings describe running-source live copy, docs also permit suspended source. No blanket SDK absence or latency guarantee.

persistent_filesystem.note: Named suspend retains root files; replacement needs an independent snapshot or explicit durable mount. Restart within 48 hours recovers latest usable snapshot only; without one filesystem is fresh. Deletion/termination wording conflicts across lifecycle, SDK and security docs. /tmp excluded from filesystem snapshots.

volumes.note: Explicit durable filesystem, up to 8 mounts; same-path writes last-writer-wins. Server autosave WAL retains newest 256 generations and all from the last 24 hours; permanent snapshots billed until deleted. Other-machine recovery reaches the last acknowledged autosave; same-machine overlay/local journal can recover unsaved work. Current session/metadata caps and precise detection/salvage/GC intervals unverified. Pins read-only/fleet-gated; invalid runtime attach can terminate sandbox. Git private WAL separate.

custom_images.note: Registered Dockerfile/SDK build or OCI import; private Docker credentials and custom USER/WORKDIR. --docker_compat fallback requires at least3x builder disk/memory. Existing filesystem snapshot registration needs Completed/durable snapshot_uri, not uploading/local-ready. Harbor public publish allowlist remains gate; full architecture/size/access matrix unresolved.

docker_in_sandbox.note: Install Docker containers and Compose support inside tensorlake/ubuntu-systemd with guest sudo/root. ubuntu-minimal lacks systemd. Harbor single-container tasks lack Docker; Compose uses a DinD host and cannot use snapshot_id.

root_sudo.note: Managed images use tl-user with passwordless sudo; command APIs permit explicit root user. Guest, not host, privileges. Custom images follow USER/WORKDIR; /workspace not writable by managed default without setup.

gpu.note: BYOC GPU fees advertised. Current SDK accepts eight model names (A100-40GB/A100-80GB/H100/T4/A6000/A10/RTX-PRO-6000/L40); defaults A10 with gpus, requires CAS image or configured GPU default and matching server/dataplane/capacity. Hosted access/limits/regions/rate unresolved; request enum or CUDA image not entitlement.

self_hosted.note: Public AWS guide installs customer executors/optional proxy but keeps Tensorlake Cloud control plane; requires project Self-hosted Compute enablement/onboarding. Enterprise advertises on-prem and security offers disconnected mode by contact; independent control-plane install/access terms unresolved.

byoc.note: AWS EC2 executors and customer S3 documented, optional customer proxy; Tensorlake Cloud scheduling/auth remains. Self-hosted Compute project enablement and onboarding required; Enterprise markets In-VPC/on-prem but exact entitlement terms unresolved. Other clouds advertised, not equivalently documented installation/access.

open_source.note: The official tensorlakeai/tensorlake repository is Apache-2.0 and includes Sandbox client/CLI plus related source components. The public sources reviewed do not establish that the full hosted Sandbox service/control plane is included or self-hostable. Partial reflects verified open-source components without overclaiming a complete open-source service; prior false inferred no-support classification was too broad for repository-level open source.

background_processes.note: start_process keeps work running after return, with signals and optional supervision. Do not assume detached CPU work resets proxy-idle timeout; suspended processes do not progress.

terminal_pty.note: SSH user keys; authenticated WebSocket PTY token; CLI ssh is PTY not native forwarding. Max64 concurrent PTYs per sandbox per create API (429), not API-rate/account-concurrency limit. Disconnected PTYs cleanup300s; whether idle-open terminals prevent sandbox idle suspension conflicts across sources.

command_streaming.note: Commands can stream stdout and stderr while they run.

secrets_management.note: Create secret_names/restore immutable-secret declarations exist, but current Python/Rust create surfaces omit secret_names; managed store/provisioning/rotation/access unverified. Ordinary env and Crabbox allowlisted per-command shell forwarding are not managed storage. Encrypted @function store remains Orchestration scope.

python_sdk.note: Lifecycle, networking, and snapshot examples use the Python sandbox SDK.

typescript_sdk.note: The same sandbox APIs are shown for TypeScript.

go_sdk.note: A separately maintained Go client exists: Sixt/tensorlake-go documents cloud sandbox create/exec, process control, PTY, suspend/resume and snapshot operations. The official Tensorlake SDK/docs inventory reviewed does not document a vendor-maintained Go Sandbox SDK; the community client is not vendor endorsement or a tested compatibility guarantee. Partial distinguishes available third-party client code from official support.

cli.note: The tl CLI creates, suspends, resumes, checkpoints, and copies sandboxes.

mcp_or_agent_integrations.note: Docs cover Harbor, Claude Managed Agents, OpenCode, Cursor Cloud Agents, Devin Outposts, and computer use.

max_vcpu.note: Pro lists 16 vCPU per sandbox. Enterprise is Custom with no higher number. Free is 1 and Usage Credits is 4.

max_memory_gib.note: Pro plan ceiling is published as 64 GB, not GiB; no silent conversion. Paid RAM ratio 1-8 GB/vCPU and plan ceiling both apply, not an entitlement to 128 GB. Lifecycle MB, API MiB and billing GiB-hours disagree; exact GiB ceiling unresolved. Enterprise custom.

max_session_duration_seconds.note: No finite cross-plan wall-clock maximum established: Pro/Enterprise unlimited, Free 2h and Usage Credits 24h published as session duration but lifecycle calls timeout_secs idle threshold. API distinguishes Free unverified 1h/verified 2h. Do not equate idle maximum with fixed active lifetime.

idle_timeout_seconds.note: Default600s proxy-idle, named suspend/ephemeral terminate. Lifecycle/open-terminal docs count connected SSH/PTY; June17 network blog counts actual bytes and says idle-open connection does not pin sandbox. Detached CPU keepalive not established. Plan verification/maxima and separate PTY300s cleanup remain; exact activity enforcement unresolved.

pricing_summary: USD hosted plans: Free $0 forever with unmetered sessions within limits; Usage Credits prepaid packs start at $5/500 CUs; Pro $250/month includes 25,000 CU then $0.01/CU overage; Enterprise custom. Usage Credits/Pro rates: CPU $0.07/$0.042 per core-hour, RAM $0.015/$0.009 per GB-hour, root disk $0.0002/$0.0001 per GB-hour, suspended snapshot storage $0.07 per GB per fixed 30-day month. Active CPU metering falls back to allocated vCPU when samples are unavailable/untrustworthy; RAM/disk allocation-based while running. Runtime measured per second; whole CUs pooled per organization, not a documented per-sandbox one-cent minimum. Hosted egress free; suspended running-resource charges stop but storage continues. GB/MB/MiB/GiB source ambiguity unresolved. Build, standalone snapshot, volume/Git storage and I/O/ingress rates are not fully published. BYOC announcement publishes CPU platform fees starting 30% of compute costs (as low as 10% at scale) and GPU 5% (as low as 2%); customer infrastructure costs extra and access/contract terms require onboarding.

pricing.conditions: USD; no credit card; unmetered sessions within 1 concurrent sandbox/1 vCPU/1 GB RAM/10 GB disk limits, not a promotional grant. Published duration 2 hours, but create API distinguishes unverified 1 hour/verified 2 hours and lifecycle treats timeout as proxy-idle threshold, not wall-clock cap. No complete Free snapshot/volume retention allowance established.

USD; no monthly fee stated. 1 CU=$0.01; $5/500 CUs, $10/1,000, $20/2,000. Up to 100 concurrent/4 vCPU/16 GB RAM/100 GB disk; published 24-hour duration is timeout maximum per lifecycle, not established wall-clock cap. Zero balance blocks new activity/stops running sandboxes rather than postpaid overage. Unused credits retained, not refunded; returning to Usage Credits requires buying a new pack.
Includes 25,000 CU, described as $250 of usage at Pro rates. Overage is $0.01 per CU. 1,000 concurrent sandboxes, 16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, unlimited session duration. Self-serve cycle is monthly.
USD marketing; unlimited concurrency/custom resource ceilings, In-VPC/on-prem/SSO/SAML/RBAC advertised. Contact/onboarding required, not a public fixed rate or ungated access.

USD; runtime measured by second. Active execution excludes idle/I/O wait only when active metering is available. Marketing pricing FAQ and pricing-limits FAQ say unavailable/untrustworthy samples fall back to allocated vCPU time for that sandbox generation; billing page itself omits fallback. No utilization assumed. Hosted rate, not BYOC infrastructure cost.

USD; runtime measured by second, active execution when metering available; unavailable/untrustworthy active samples fall back to allocated vCPU time for sandbox generation. No utilization inferred; price item retains its own qualification independent of other receipts.
Allocation-based while the sandbox is running. The same billing doc says the usage tab shows GiB-hours.

Billed while suspended. Pricing page says a fixed 30-day month. Enterprise is custom. The docs do not say whether a memory-preserving suspend bills filesystem size, filesystem plus RAM, or measured artifact size.

pricing.published_price: No running CPU, RAM or root-disk charge while suspended
pricing.conditions: Named sandboxes only; preserved state still billed as snapshot storage at $0.07/GB-month. Waiting while running still incurs RAM/root-disk allocation, with CPU fallback possible; suspend is not free retained storage.

research_notes: GB, GiB, MB, and MiB are all used for memory or disk across the pricing page, billing doc, and lifecycle doc. Rates were copied as published and not converted.
Active CPU billing depends on measured execution, with an allocated-vCPU fallback. No utilization figure was inferred.
Snapshot storage size for a memory-preserving suspend and standalone checkpoint/volume/Git storage charge details were not specified; missing rates are not free.

Sandbox create OpenAPI secret_names and GPU model/count fields are leads, not full managed-secret or hosted GPU availability evidence. Orchestration secrets are a separate product scope; BYOC GPU commercial claim remains gated.

Official sources conflict on termination/restart/deletion, proxy-idle versus session/lifetime caps, live Cloud Hypervisor resource resizing/pool disk configuration, public image publishing gates, and dynamic egress update/hostname behavior. Fact notes preserve those conflicts for selected-control packets.
